name: Xero
tagline: Cloud accounting, invoicing, bank reconciliation, payroll add-ons, and reporting

verdictSummary: Invoices and reports are buildable, but Xero's real product is bank feeds, accounting workflows, accountant collaboration, compliance expectations, integrations, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Build simple bookkeeping with invoices, expenses, CSV imports, chart of accounts, and reports for personal/internal use.

notes: Another structural no due regulatory/financial integrations.
prompt:
Honest answer: don't. Xero's product is not the ledger UI, it is bank
feeds, reconciliation, payroll and tax integrations, and books your accountant
will accept. A vibecoded clone of that gambles with your actual finances, and
the compliance surface never stops moving.

If you need real accounting without the subscription, run Odoo or Invoice Ninja
(links in prior art) and keep the accountant.

If what you actually need is freelancer-grade bookkeeping, here's the weekend
version:

- A local web app (Node + Express + better-sqlite3): income and expense entries
  with date, amount, category, client, and an attached receipt file.
- CSV import from my bank's export, plus a rules table (description pattern to
  category) so repeat transactions auto-categorize.
- Invoices numbered sequentially, rendered to PDF with pdfkit, one paid/unpaid
  flag. Nothing more.
- Reports: quarterly income, expenses by category, and a one-page cash P&L I can
  print for my accountant.
- Binds to localhost only, no telemetry; nightly copy of the SQLite file to a
  dated backup.

What you will NOT have: bank feeds, reconciliation, payroll, tax filing, audit
history, or numbers anyone will sign off unchecked. Use it to stay organized
between real tools, not instead of them.
